content.text: Let me check what issue is on line 84 of the admin page more carefully. I notice there's an h2 with class "text-h3" which might be the issue:

Perfect! I've found the issue. Let me analyze my findings: ## Analysis of the WCAG/§4 Audit Finding **THE FINDING IS INCOMPLETE — there IS a genuine accessibility issue that was missed:** ### What I Found: 1. **Correct heading hierarchy (lines 41-70)**: ✓ - One `

` via DashboardHeader (line 21 of DashboardHeader.tsx) - Three `

` elements for 'Strategic', 'Operational', and 'Alerts' sections (lines 47, 59, 70) - Proper skip-link implementation in root layout (app/layout.tsx, lines 39-44) 2. **ACTUAL ISSUE - Semantic/Hierarchy Violation (line 84)**: - The "Config" section uses `

{t("admin.configHeading")}

` - This is a **semantic error**: it's an `

` HTML element styled as a `text-h3`, not visually styled to match the other h2s - This breaks heading hierarchy consistency — after three h2s at the same level, suddenly there's another h2 but styled smaller - The heading hierarchy becomes confusing: h1, h2, h2, h2, then h2 (but visually h3), with no h3 anywhere else - **This violates WCAG 2.1 Level A (1.3.1 Info and Relationships) and Level AA (2.4.10 Section Headings)** — the visual hierarchy doesn't match the semantic hierarchy 3. **The skip-link implementation is correct** — targets `#main` which is properly set in the layout. ### Why This Is Real: - Screen reader users will hear four h2s at the same level, but visually the last one appears smaller (like an h3), creating confusion - The visual/semantic mismatch is a genuine accessibility and usability problem - This violates the principle that visual hierarchy should match DOM hierarchy true The audit claim that "the structure is correct" is incomplete. While the skip-link and main h1→h2 hierarchy are correct, line 84 contains a genuine semantic violation:

breaks heading hierarchy consistency by using mismatched semantic (h2) and visual (h3) levels. This violates WCAG 2.1 Level A (1.3.1 Info and Relationships), creating a confusing experience for screen reader users who hear h2 but see h3 visual styling.
